article.title: Displaced Kurds Return to Destroyed Homes in Northeast Syria
paras: Editor's note: This story was adapted from the original Kurdish video story.
After more than seven years of displacement, Daham Ibrahim is finally preparing to return home in the countryside of Sere Kaniye (Ras al-Ayn) in northeast Syria.
Ibrahim, who had hoped that his tent would become nothing more than a painful memory of the past, is now taking it with him to set it up on the site where his house once stood.

“I’m returning to my village, but I have no choice but to set up this tent at the same place where my house used to be,” Ibrahim, a father of eight, told VOA. “My house was destroyed during the war. Our village used to have 500 houses; now barely 100 houses are intact.”

Ibrahim is one of many who were displaced during a 2019 Turkish-led offensive against the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), a former U.S. partner in the fight against the Islamic State terror group.
Since last August, thousands of displaced people in northeast Syria have been returning home as part of an integration process between the interim Syrian government and the SDF.
According to Syrian government officials, more than 4,000 families have returned to the Sere Kaniye region. But, like Ibrahim, most returnees are going back to destroyed or damaged houses.
To help compensate for these losses, the Syrian government is providing each returning family with $2,000 in assistance. But many say the amount isn't enough to rebuild their homes.
At displacement camps, those still waiting to return home hope that authorities will expedite the process, especially as a harsh winter approaches.
“We have endured seven years of hunger and cold. It is time for us to go back home,” said Fatima Habash, another displaced person from Sere Kaniye.
“We yearn for a normal life. The government needs to remove those people who are living in our houses, so that we can return to them,” she told VOA.

Before the fall of the Bashar al-Assad regime in December 2024, Sere Kaniye was under the control of Turkish-backed Syrian armed groups. Although those groups have since integrated into the Syrian ministry of defense, their continued presence, along with that of their families living in houses of displaced residents, has made it difficult for many to return.
Mahmoud Khalil, deputy commander of the Internal Security Forces in Hasaka province, said efforts are underway to remove families currently occupying the homes of Sere Kaniye residents.
“If everything goes according to plan, we should be able to facilitate the return of 1,000 people to the city within a month,” Khalil told VOA.

The Sere Kaniye Displaced Persons Committee, a civil society group advocating for displaced people in northeast Syria, this week said that returning home is a fundamental right for displaced people, particularly now that in its view, the Syrian conflict has ended.
The group called on Syrian authorities to ensure the safe and voluntary return of people still living in displacement camps.
zh: 流離失所的庫德族人返回敘利亞東北部遭毀的家中
編者註：本報導改編自原版的庫德語影片報導。
流離失所超過七年之後，達哈姆·易卜拉欣終於準備返回位於敘利亞東北部塞雷卡尼耶（拉斯艾因）鄉間的家鄉。
伊布拉希姆原本希望這頂帳篷能僅僅成為過去的一段痛苦回憶，但現在他卻將它帶在身邊，準備在曾經是自家房屋所在的地方搭起這頂帳篷。
「我正要回到我的村子，但別無選擇，只能在以前我家所在的地方搭起這頂帳篷，」育有八名子女的伊布拉希姆告訴美國之音。「我的房子在戰爭中被摧毀了。我們村子以前有500間房子；現在完好無損的房子不到100間。」
易卜拉欣是眾多在2019年土耳其主導的對抗庫德族領導的「敘利亞民主力量」（SDF）的攻勢中流離失所的人士之一；該組織曾是美國在打擊「伊斯蘭國」恐怖組織行動中的合作夥伴。
自去年八月以來，作為敘利亞臨時政府與「敘利亞民主力量」（SDF）之間融合進程的一部分，敘利亞東北部數千名流離失所者已陸續返鄉。
據敘利亞政府官員表示，已有超過 4,000 戶家庭返回塞雷卡尼耶地區。然而，就像易卜拉欣一樣，大多數返鄉者回到的是已被摧毀或受損的房屋。
為了彌補這些損失，敘利亞政府正向每戶返鄉家庭提供 2,000 美元的援助。但許多人表示，這筆金額不足以讓他們重建家園。
在流離失所者營地裡，那些仍在等待返鄉的人們希望當局能加快相關程序，尤其是隨著嚴冬將至。
「我們已經忍受了七年的飢寒交迫。現在是時候回家了，」來自塞雷卡尼耶的另一名流離失所者法蒂瑪·哈巴什說道。
「我們渴望過上正常的生活。政府必須將那些佔據我們房屋的人趕走，這樣我們才能回到自己的家裡，」她對美國之音表示。
在2024年12月巴沙爾·阿薩德政權垮台之前，塞雷卡尼耶一直由土耳其支持的敘利亞武裝團體控制。 儘管這些武裝團體此後已併入敘利亞國防部，但他們持續駐紮於此，加上其家屬居住在流離失所居民的房屋中，使得許多人難以返鄉。
哈塞克省內部安全部隊副指揮官馬哈茂德·哈利勒表示，目前正著手將目前佔據塞雷卡尼耶居民住宅的家庭遷出。
「如果一切按計畫進行，我們應該能在一個月內協助 1,000 人返回該市，」哈利勒告訴美國之音。
「塞雷·卡尼耶流離失所者委員會」——一個致力於為敘利亞東北部流離失所者發聲的公民社會團體——本週表示，返回家園是流離失所者的基本權利，特別是鑒於該組織認為，敘利亞衝突現已結束。
該組織呼籲敘利亞當局確保仍居住在流離失所者營地的人們能夠安全且自願地返回家園。
